findings.title: Autoreleased NSData leaks per BLE write chunk on managed threads

confidence.rationale: Traced the write path in source; Apple documents convenience constructors as autoreleasing; .NET threads provably lack autorelease pools. Not executed on hardware (no mac host).

findings.symptom: WriteAsync creates one NSData per chunk via dataWithBytes:length: (autoreleasing) on a .NET thread with no autorelease pool
findings.consequence: A print job pushes tens of KB in 20-512 byte chunks: hundreds of leaked NSData objects per label on the golden print path; unbounded growth across a print session
findings.remedy: Use alloc + initWithBytes:length: (owned reference) and objc_release after writeValue; audit all convenience-constructor uses on managed threads
findings.verification: Falsifier: run a print on macOS under Instruments/leaks and observe NSData count stable across labels after the fix

findings.title: Delegate released while CoreBluetooth can still dispatch to it (use-after-free)

confidence.rationale: Traced both cleanup paths in source; CBCentralManager/CBPeripheral delegates are weak per Apple docs, so our alloc is the sole strong ref; sibling path (ScanAsync finally) shares the mechanism.

findings.symptom: CleanupAsync releases the delegate without first detaching it from central/peripheral; ScanAsync finally block likewise destroys the delegate right after stopScan
findings.consequence: A callback already queued on the GCD queue is delivered to a deallocated ObjC object: native crash of the host app (managed-side Owners map cannot protect the ObjC receiver)
findings.remedy: setDelegate:nil on peripheral and central after cancel/stop, then release the delegate; mirror the order in ScanAsync
findings.verification: Falsifier: on macOS, connect/disconnect in a tight loop with notifications flowing; no crash after fix, crash reproducible before fix under ASan

findings.title: Managed exception escaping [UnmanagedCallersOnly] callbacks crashes the process

confidence.rationale: Runtime fail-fast for managed exceptions crossing UnmanagedCallersOnly frames is documented .NET behavior; callback bodies allocate, lock, and log, all of which can throw.

findings.symptom: All ten delegate IMPs route into owner logic (list ops, objc_retain, tracing) with no try/catch at the native boundary
findings.source: src/Niimbot.Net/Transport/MacOS/CoreBluetoothDelegate.cs: `private static void DidDiscover(IntPtr self, IntPtr sel, ...) => Owner(self)?.OnPeripheralDiscovered(peripheral);`
findings.consequence: Any managed throw inside a CoreBluetooth callback terminates the whole host application rather than failing one connect
findings.remedy: Wrap each routed callback body in try/catch; route failures to Fail()/NiimbotTrace, never across the native boundary
findings.verification: Falsifier: inject a throwing owner callback in a mac test harness; process survives and the connect fails gracefully after the fix

rejectedFindings.title: _central field read race in discovery callback

confidence.rationale: Traced ordering in source: scan starts only from the state callback, which itself uses the passed central pointer.

rejectedFindings.consequence: None in practice: field assignment completes before any scan starts; discovery arrives milliseconds later
rejectedFindings.verification: Ordering argument recorded; would only matter if scan started before init returned, which CoreBluetooth does not do

rejectedFindings.title: setNotifyValue: overload ambiguity (int literal to sbyte vs nint)

confidence.rationale: Build compiles green; ABI analysis shows identical register usage at this arity either way.

rejectedFindings.symptom: Int literals 0/1 passed where sbyte and IntPtr overloads both exist
rejectedFindings.consequence: None: BOOL reads the low byte of the same argument register regardless of chosen overload
rejectedFindings.verification: Verified by successful compile + arm64/x64 calling convention analysis

rejectedFindings.title: Duplicate ObjC class-name registration across AssemblyLoadContexts

confidence.rationale: Pattern-match on objc_allocateClassPair semantics; double-load scenario not sampled.

rejectedFindings.symptom: objc_allocateClassPair returns null for a duplicate name; code throws
rejectedFindings.consequence: Exotic plugin/double-load scenarios fail loudly at first connect with a clear exception, not silently
rejectedFindings.remedy: Accept: loud failure is adequate for this edge
rejectedFindings.verification: Would need a two-ALC repro to justify complexity of a randomized class name

rejectedFindings.title: AsyncByteQueue spurious 0-return under reader/writer race

confidence.rationale: Executed the cross-thread stream test (16 KiB, unaligned chunks) which exercises the race window.

rejectedFindings.symptom: Semaphore rebalance can consume a count belonging to an in-flight writer
rejectedFindings.consequence: A mid-stream 0 return, which the transport read contract explicitly allows (0 = idle; client pump re-polls)
